report.source_text: Following an evaluation by a medical oncologist and a series of careful discussions about the likely outcomes and risks of treatment, our patient consented to undergo a treatment course of cytotoxic chemotherapy for his symptomatic visceral KS. Cardiac MRI performed 4 weeks into the admission following initiation of cART showed normalisation of left ventricular function, indicating either interobserver variability in the initial study or a reversible cardiomyopathy induced by either direct myocardial viral invasion or malnutrition. Nonetheless, in light of a perceived risk of future myocardial dysfunction given the initial echocardiography, single-agent, weekly paclitaxel was selected for his chemotherapeutic regimen, rather than conventional (or indeed liposomal) doxorubicin.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 30-year-old heterosexual man presented in May 2020 with a 4-day history of dry cough, exertional dyspnea, and hypoxia (SpO2 92%) in the context of marked systemic findings: disseminated pigmented rash on torso, extensive non-tender cervical lymphadenopathy, severe lower limb and scrotal edema, marked cachexia (45 kg) with year-long weight loss, and tachycardia (117 bpm). Chest radiograph revealed extensive bilateral airspace opacification. HIV serology was positive with severely depressed CD4+ count of 116 cells/μL (9%) and high viral load of 87,272 copies/mL, indicating advanced AIDS. CT-guided biopsy of an iliac crest lesion demonstrated spindle cell proliferation strongly positive for CD34 and HHV-8 on immunohistochemistry, confirming Kaposi sarcoma with bone involvement. The patient was initiated on combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) and weekly paclitaxel chemotherapy. Cardiac MRI at 4 weeks showed normalization of left ventricular function. Over the 3-month admission, the patient demonstrated clinical response with improvement in peripheral edema, weight, and oxygenation. By June 2021, viral load was consistently suppressed, CD4+ count had recovered to 221 cells/μL (15%), and the patient had returned to a healthy weight.
